name: Proof of Human
long_description:
Proof of Human is an API that invisibly detects bots and verifies human identity.

Founded by Princeton cognitive scientists, Proof of Human leverages world-class research with industry-beating benchmarks so platforms can verify their human users friction-free.
one_liner: continuous human verification without CAPTCHAs or user friction

founders.founder_bio:
CEO of Proof of Human, building the invisible Turing Test for the Internet. 

Before Proof of Human, Mayank completed a PhD at Princeton University working at the intersection of cognitive science and artificial intelligence, publishing in high-impact venues including Science, PNAS, and Psychological Review.

founders.title: Founder
founders.founder_bio: Matt is a co-founder of Proof of Human, a company building the invisible Turing Test for the internet. Before Proof of Human, Matt was a PhD student at Princeton University, where he used machine learning and behavioral and experiments to study how people make decisions. Before his PhD, Matt majored in both statistics and economics at the University of Toronto, and worked in data science and econometrics.

launches.title: Proof of Human, PBC: The invisible Turing Test for the Internet
launches.tagline: The Proof of Human API continuously distinguishes humans from bots and AI agents.
launches.body:
**The internet is losing the ability to know who is human.**

AI agents can now browse websites, fill out forms, complete tasks, and produce responses that are increasingly difficult to distinguish from those of real people. The systems the internet has historically relied on to separate humans from machines were not built for this world.

## PROOF OF HUMAN

The Proof of Human API continuously distinguishes humans from bots and AI agents.\
\
Modern AI can produce very human-like outputs. But producing an answer and producing it like a human are different things. Humans hesitate. We make mistakes. We correct ourselves. Our attention changes over time. The way we type, move, and interact leaves rich signatures that remain difficult for AI systems to reproduce. We call the broader research program _the Invisible Turing Test for the Internet_.

Proof of Human runs in the background while someone uses a website—no CAPTCHA, no puzzle, no interruption. We combine behavioral, device, and network signals and return a real-time assessment that companies can use to decide whether to trust an account, accept a response, or pay for work.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=swJabsQubf4>

## BENCHMARKS

We tested scripted bots and AI agents against Proof of Human and other leading detection systems.  

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117699&key=user_uploads/1202145/ae031489-b618-4c0f-a1e7-a68dfa8cca03)

_On a five-question survey, Proof of Human identified 99% of automated sessions, followed by reCAPTCHA v3 at 69.4%, hCaptcha at 44.3%, Cloudflare Turnstile at 42.1%, and Cloudflare Bot Management at 9.1%._

Traditional automation signals remain effective against scripted browsers, but they are less reliable when AI agents operate through genuine browser environments. Even interactive challenges may offer limited protection when vision-capable agents can interpret and complete them. As browser-level indicators become easier to avoid, the way a user behaves throughout a session becomes increasingly important for distinguishing human activity from automation.

## OUR CUSTOMERS

**Today, Proof of Human acts as the trust layer behind online human research.** Stanford Psychology uses it to verify that participants in online studies are real. GrowProgress uses it as part of its quality-control stack for polling and public-opinion research. Market insights firms including Obsurvant use it to identify AI agents and other fraudulent respondents before they enter client datasets.\
\
The common problem is the same: a response itself is no longer enough. An AI agent can give a coherent answer, pass an attention check, and look perfectly legitimate in the final dataset. Proof of Human looks at the process that produced it—how someone types, clicks, scrolls, moves through a page, and interacts with their device—continuously and without interrupting the user.\
\
Production traffic also teaches us what to look for next. Customer deployments have uncovered new patterns of automation, from unnatural typing to partial AI copy-pasting, that are difficult or impossible to identify from the final answer alone. Those behaviors become new detectors, which are then tested across human, bot, and agent traffic before being deployed back into the network. The result is a system that improves as the adversary changes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117699&key=user_uploads/1202145/0f53b0f4-ec5e-4837-acec-549a275ac727)

_Proof of Human at Stanford Psychology. We first encountered this problem as researchers ourselves; today, research groups use Proof of Human to verify that the people behind online studies are actually people._

## THE FUTURE

We started with online research because the problem was acute and measurable: organizations were paying for human judgment without reliably knowing whether a human had produced it.

But the same problem is rapidly appearing across applications, marketplaces, transactions, social platforms, and digital work. The internet needs a way to know when a human is actually on the other side—continuously, invisibly, and without another CAPTCHA.

Welcome to the Proof of Human era.

Matt & Mayank
